1.definition: Greek for "the Empire of the Romans" (basih-LAY-ah tone roh-MY-ohn) — the name the Byzantines actually used for their own state. They never said "Byzantine"; they were Romaioi, Romans, and their polity was the Roman Empire continued in the Greek-speaking east.

"You have conquered, Galilean" — the dying words attributed (almost certainly apocryphally) to the emperor Julian the Apostate, conceding that Christianity had defeated his attempt to restore Greco-Roman paganism. "Galilean" is a dismissive pagan term for Christ.

2.definition: Latin for "I have read" — the single word the hostile source Procopius claims the semi-literate Justin I had cut into a stencil so he could trace it to sign documents. No friendly source confirms the story; it may be pure invective.

5.definition: "On the Themes" — a tenth-century geographical-administrative treatise compiled under Constantine VII describing the empire's military provinces (themes). It is now judged partly inaccurate and antiquarian, but it preserves administrative detail recorded nowhere else.

Old Slavic for "word" or "utterance" — the root that gave the Glagolitic alphabet its name. Cyril built the script around the actual sound system of Slavic, the first writing ever devised specifically for the language.

Old Norse for "sworn companions" — the word behind "Varangian." It named the Scandinavian and Rus' warriors bound by oath of service, the recruiting pool for the Byzantine emperor's elite Varangian Guard.

6.definition: The Byzantine emperor's crown — an arched, jeweled cap set with precious stones, with strings of pearls dangling down beside the wearer's face. Part of the formal imperial regalia.
The emperor's private viewing box at the Constantinople hippodrome, linked by a hidden staircase to the Great Palace so he could watch the chariot races and slip in and out without facing the crowd.
The deepest grades of purple silk, a state monopoly reserved for the emperor's use. It was colored with murex purple, a costly dye made using techniques the Byzantines inherited from the Phoenicians.
Greek for "consul of the philosophers" — the head of higher philosophical study at Constantinople, a state-appointed senior chair. Michael Psellos famously held it in the eleventh century.

10.definition: Greek for "stillness" or "inner quiet" — the contemplative silence at the heart of Hesychasm: continuous interior prayer, stilling the mind, aimed at direct experience of God's uncreated light.
